chapters.html:
"Are you my master?"

Phainon dropped his keys. There's a stranger sitting on his couch. No, sitting is not the right word. Spreading, more like. He looked like he had every right to be here. Phainon considered calling the police. But there was no sign of forced entry in his apartment, and the man didn't seem to be violent. He scanned the room for anything he could use for self-defence if needed be. He's confident in his physical abilities to fight off most people, but not this one.

"Who are you and what are you doing in my home?"

The man looked like he walked straight out of a history drama. Phainon shouldn't stare at his bare chest, but he did anyway.

"You summoned me, didn't you?"

"I did?"

Silence fell between them.

"I...materialized here somehow. I thought that must be why."

"Materialized? Are you...some kind of spirit?"

"You can say that."

Phainon pinched himself hard to make sure he wasn't dreaming. He really wasn't.

"Ah, this must be some kind of mistake." He tried to clear his head, "I didn't summon you. I don't even know how to."

The man — the spirit gave him a pointed look.

"You have the command spells on your hand. The mark of Strife. My mark." He said, as if that's all the clarification necessary.

"Command spells?" Phainon lifted his left hand and froze mid-action.

"You really have no idea what's going on, do you?"

"I'm afraid you'll need to fill me in." Phainon sat down himself. Somehow he felt his guard relax, "maybe start with the part where you called me your master?"

"I'm not going to actually call you that." The spirit sighed, but then he gave Phainon an overview of the holy grail war.

"So if I don't tell you my name, can you call me master?"

"I just told you there's a war coming and you could die, and that's your takeaway?"

"Oh, I'm definitely trying to not panic over the possibility of dying here."

"Perhaps you're underestimating the power of a heroic spirit, Phainon ."

Phainon didn't realize how the way he said his name made his heart skip a beat.

"That's not fair," he pouted, "so how should I address you?"

"You can call me Mydeimos."

"Mydeimos." Phainon repeated. Why did that sound so familiar? Then he practically screamed, "the God of Strife? The undying prince of Castrum Kremnos?"

"Lancer class." Mydeimos nodded. "Good, that saves me trouble explaining."

"You must be really powerful." Phainon was star-struck.

"Considering you have no idea what's going on, I'm glad I'm powerful enough for the both of us."

"Hey, I'm not useless!" Phainon protested, "I can fight too! And I'm the debate champion at uni!"

"You won't know what to do against servants, I'd like to see you talk your way out of that." Mydeimos said, "and by the way, you stare too much."

"Don't blame me. People in our era don't dress like that."

"Your loss then."

"You know what," Phainon licked his lips, "I completely agree."

"...How did I get stuck with you?"

"Maybe you're unlucky?"

Mydeimos groaned.

"Okay, you don't have to act so disappointed." Phainon raised his hands, "it's not like I actually signed up for this."

Mydeimos thought for a moment.

"I'll keep you alive." He said authoritatively, "you have nothing to be afraid of."

"Wow," Phainon blinked, "so you do want to keep me around."

"Nope, I just hate losing."

Phainon couldn't help but laugh, and to his surprise, Mydeimos chuckled to himself.

Phainon came home to a clean, well-organized apartment. Mydeimos was in the kitchen, there's a pot simmering on the stove, the content of which made heaven smell like a gas station convenience store in comparison.

"You know, when you said 'servant', I didn’t expect a live-in maid." Phainon was very impressed.

"Mind your tongue," Mydeimos raised an eyebrow, "you are speaking to the last king of Castrum Kremnos."

"Uh-huh, you do realize you're not quite making the point you think you are, dressed in a pink apron half naked like that?"

"Getting familiar already, aren't you?" Mydeimos crossed his arms.

"I think," Phainon gestured at the room, "you're the one who's getting very comfortable around here."

"That's because the state of your living quarters is what corrupts the minds of a warrior—"

"You're acting tough. You don't even like to title drop," Phainon smirked.

"What do you even know about me?"

"Well, you don't think I won't do any background check on the mysterious hot man who appeared in my room, right?"

Mydeimos scoffed.

"I've told you what you need to know."

"Oh, I very much doubt that," Phainon grinned, "you see, there's this particularly interesting branch of history—"

"Don't tell me you've been reading those fabricated lies—"

"—It says that you make great food, play with kids, and draw cute chimeras."

"..."

"I can see the first part is true" Phainon declared victory, "if you tell me if the rest are, you get these—as a prize."

He lifted up his grocery bag, showing Mydeimos the bottles of pomegranate juice.

"Fine," Mydeimos grunted, "they were true. Give me those."

"Wow, I was expecting a harder fight."

"There's nothing wrong for a warrior to indulge in simple pleasure, especially in times of war."

"And what other simple pleasures would you like to indulge in?"

Mydeimos didn't dignify that with a response.

"You accepted all this really well." He said.

"I've surprised myself, if I'm being honest." Phainon said, "but somehow I don't mind you here at all. I don't know why though, you feel...familiar."

Mydeimos studied Phainon's face.

"What's your wish?" He asked.

"My wish?"

"For the grail. What would you ask of the grail?"

Phainon seemed genuinely confused.

"Gotta admit, haven't thought about it." He scratched his head, "everything's good in the village, everyone I know is doing well, so I guess there's nothing for me to ask for."

"What about for yourself?"

"Well," he blushed, "maybe, maybe I want to find love. But that's not the kind of thing you ask the grail for, is it?"

"...I suppose not."

"Then what about you? You must have a wish, that's why you're here, right?"

Mydeimos hesitated.

"Come on, I've told you my embarrassing secret."

It was a long shot. Phainon didn't expect Mydeimos to offer a response. But then he spoke.

"I'm looking for someone." There was sorrow in his voice. 

Phainon waited for him to continue. 

"We were fighting together, against the end of our world. But he disappeared, after the world was saved."

"Why?"

"Did you know this world was once locked in a cycle, repeating itself for over 33 million times?"

"This...this world?"

Mydeimos sighed. “You don’t know. As I expected. No one knows this part of history anymore.” 

“I…can’t imagine.” 

“He killed me 33 million times.”

“...” Phainon didn’t know what to say, then he took Mydeimos’ hands, and looked him in the eye solemnly, “I’m sorry. I will help you get your revenge, in all my powers. I swear.” 

“Who said I want revenge?” Mydeimos shot him a strange look. 

“...What?” Phainon’s mouth was wide open.

“I want to bring him home. And I want his name to be remembered. His name, Khaslana , should not fade away like this. “ 

His sword pierced through Mydeimos' back. Golden blood stained his hand, dripping down to the ground, silent but deafening. The king fell to the ground, the fire from battle yet to fade from his eyes.

"Become the dawn, deliverer." The king breathed his last.

He walked past the body without looking back. No pain. No remorse. He kept on walking, surrounded by complete darkness, golden blood from his sword leaving a trail on the ground, marking the way he came from.

Keep going. He heard his own voice.

But what am I looking for?

You will find the answer. The voice said. You must reach within.

Who are you? He asked.

Khaslana. The voice murmured.

And then he saw a ray of light shining through the dark. He reached out. He ran. He sprinted until the light embraced him.

Then he found Mydeimos lifeless on the ground again.

Phainon shot up from his bed, breathing heavily, his body sticky with sweat, which felt a lot like how the blood covered him in his dreams. Someone was calling his name, but his mind was not ready to come back to reality. Everything around him felt distorted.

It took him a minute to realize Mydeimos was sitting next to him in bed, an arm around his shoulder, and he was practically leaning against his bare chest. He jumped.

"You don't look well." Mydeimos frowned, holding him in place.

"I'm fine. It's just a nightmare." Phainon managed to say.

"You've been having a lot of nightmares lately."

"It's no big deal. I've just been...stressed. I've told you how professor Anaxa can be about deadlines." Phainon shrugged, lying through his teeth. He didn't know how much Mydeimos could feel through their shared bond. Given that Mydeimos could still maintain his physical form in this world, the connection should be stable enough. But the truth is, he had been feeling a lot more fatigued than usual, partially due to these recurring nightmares. What's more, there was a pain shooting from his chest, coursing through his body. It was like there's something draining him from within, something threatening to surface and take control.

He had never been more scared, but he would not let himself be defeated by fear. Or anything. He could not collapse. He wanted to fulfill Mydeimos' wish. And his dreams were his only clue. None of his research on Khaslana had yielded any results.

Mydeimos did not seem convinced at all.

"I'm going to scan the premises," he said, "we could be under attack. Probably by the servants who never dare to show their faces in a fight." He gritted through his teeth.

Phainon shook his head weakly.

"No, that could be just what the enemy wants. To lure you away and take me out."

The argument was compelling enough and Mydeimos had to agree.

"I'll get you some water then."

But Phainon grabbed his wrist before he could get up.

"Don't go." He whispered, still staring a hole into his blanket.

He could tell that surprised Mydeimos. His body acted before his mind. How could he let Mydeimos close to him, when he'd been the one killing Mydeimos over and over in his dreams?

But he needed to see Mydeimos here. Alive. Breathing. He was gripping too hard, and he wasn't ready to let go.

"I'll be here." Mydeimos said, his voice more gentle than Phainon had ever heard, "sleep. I'll be here when you wake up."

Phainon closed his eyes and relaxed into Mydeimos' embrace. He would figure out what those dreams mean, but not now. Right now, he just needed to feel Mydeimos' warm body pressed against him, so he could tell himself the dreams aren't real. He barely felt a light kiss pressed on his hair before his consciousness faded away.

Mydeimos did not want to leave, but Phainon sent him grocery shopping. He made those big puppy eyes and said he wanted the honeycakes Mydeimos made when he woke up, and Mydeimos could not say no. Not in any lifetime.

He double checked the protective barrier he set up around the building. But when he returned, Phainon was nowhere to be found.

He felt as if all his blood had turned into ice. The bond between them was growing weaker and weaker, but Mydeimos was still able to track it. A good sign , he tried to reassure himself.

Then he found a white-haired figure, lying face down on the ground of the park nearby. Phainon didn't seem to be moving, and Mydeimos wasn't sure if he was breathing at all until he pulled him into his own arms. There were no wounds on him, his breath was weak and labored, but at least he's alive.

"Phainon," he cried out in desperation, " Phainon . Stay with me."

He cursed himself for letting Phainon trick him into leaving his side. He could fight ten thousands of enemies, but what could he do when Phainon fainted in his arms like this? His fingers clung to Phainon's shirt, turning his knuckles white.

As if heard his call, Phainon's body tensed up, and he let out a scream as if he was just pulled out from the deepest dark. He was shaking uncontrollably. His eyes were blank, as if fixated on something that does not exist in space and time.

"Mydeimos." Phainon's lips moved, his words barely audible.

"Don't talk. I'll get help." Mydeimos didn't have time to feel relieved. But Phainon put a hand on his arms, almost reassuringly, to stop him from going anywhere.

"What...did you do?" Mydeimos heard the tremble in his own voice.

"You know those dreams I've been having? They were leading me to the truth. The truth about...us."

"What are you not telling me?"

"Do you know how many times I killed you in my dreams?"

There was no emotion in Phainon's voice. It was as if they were talking about the TV show that made them fall asleep next to each other. In fact, there's no emotion in his eyes either. No expression on his face. All the color had faded from his life.

No. He shouldn't have to go through this too.

Phainon continued, "I don't know how I got stuck in the cycle, but I had to break it. And I had to believe that as long as I keep going, I will reach a different end."

"There's a voice that keeps telling me: You must reach within. And now, I have seen it. I know how to fix everything now."

He raised his hand with all that's left of his strength.

"Mydeimos, by the power of command spells, I order you—"

"No! Phainon!"

"Put your hand through my heart—"

"Stop!"

He tried to fight against it, but it was too late. His body no longer belonged to him. A taste of blood erupted from his mouth. His gauntlet pierced through Phainon's skin easily. Too easily.

"Why?!"

"Because...I want to fulfill your wish."

"My wish," Mydeimos cried in despair, "is to see you living a happy life. In a different life. In every life."

His fingers tightened around a cold object in Phainon's now hollow chest, and his heart sank. Golden light shined from the void that once hosted Phainon's heart.

The holy grail.

"Ah, but you see," Phainon's mouth twisted into a bitter laugh, "I'm not real. I'm but a vessel."

Then his body went limp as if he let go of all that tethered him to life. Mydeimos screamed his name over and over, but there was nothing he could do. The grail glowed warm gold, too blinding through his tears, the light poured out from it, encasing Phainon's lifeless body, lifting it midair, out of Mydeimos' reach.

Then something changed. First it was wings. Giant wings, one gold, one dark, emerged from the cocoon of light. Then the light dissipated, and a familiar figure descended upon him.

"Mydeimos." He greeted, voice deep.

"Phainon... no, Khaslana?"

No. This was too much. Phainon just died by his hand, and he pulled out the holy grail from his body, and now Khaslana. His Phainon. His Khaslana who disappeared for millenia.

So he did the only thing he could, which was to stop thinking at all. He had to do something before the guilt, anger, and grief exploded inside him. Thunders raged around him, tearing up the sky. Spears of crimson crystals formed at his hand and launched at the person he missed the most.

"How?!" He screamed when Khaslana parried yet another attack from him. "I've searched for you, for eternity—"

"I'm sorry we have to meet again like this, Mydeimos."

"Phainon didn't deserve this—"

"No, he didn't." Khaslana sighed, "but he found me."

Mydei couldn't hold back his anger, and he wasn't going to.

"You've been hiding in the grail...inside him?"

"I locked our world into endless cycles, and I'd killed you many, many times." Khaslana said, as if narrating someone else's story, "Then the grail appeared. I didn't know how, but I had to try anything."

He continued, "I wanted to fulfill everyone's wishes. I owed you all that much at least, after everything. I wished to correct the curse in our existence. I wanted everyone to be free. To become real lives."

Mydeimos slowed his attack. It was as if something was twisting his insides.

"But the grail never grants wishes the way you expect. Before I realized, I...fused with it, and I became the will of it, but at the same time, I was trapped in it. It became a labyrinth made from my past memories, and Phainon...Phainon got through it to find me."

"You mean you let it trap you. You made it your own prison." Mydeimos said it coldly.

Khaslana averted his eyes.

"You thought it was easier, you thought you deserve it, so you wouldn't have to face what you did to us, to me—"

"You don't get to say that." Khaslana raised his voice, "you can't possibly know how I felt."

But when Mydeimos attacked him again, he didn't fight back. He let the spear pierce his shoulder and let him pin him onto the ground.

"You're right I don't know how you feel." Mydeimos met his eyes, "but I know enough about your wish."

"My wish? My wish was fulfilled. Our world was saved."

"Then tell me. Why are you here? Why am I here?"

Khaslana opened his mouth but no words came out.

"Still can't be honest with yourself? Shall I try?" Mydeimos trapped him with his own body. He leaned in, their lips only an inch away, and Mydeimos said every word slowly and deliberately, "you said the grail never granted wish the way you expect. You wanted a way out, and it gave you exactly that. That's why the grail appeared. There was no war, no other servants, because it only listened to you. And it made the Phainon of this world into its vessel."

He paused, then declared without mercy, "all because you missed me."

Then he claimed his lips like he claimed victory. It was war like all their fights. Heated, primal, devastating. Mydeimos fought for his win, his lost love and grief, and Khaslana responded with longing of millenia.

"You beat me." Khaslana smiled when they finally parted.

It was the first time Mydeimos saw him smile. He could taste the bittersweet feeling in his mouth.

"I've missed that."

"Still," Khaslana said, "even though I was your Phainon once, I cannot go back to just being your Phainon."

Mydeimos picked up the grail. Crimson crystals emerged from the surface. Then with a crack, the grail crumbled into pieces.

"Now you have nowhere to hide again."

Khaslana chuckled, "I'm the will of the grail. I can make a new one if I wanted to."

"Well, will you?" Mydeimos challenged, "go on then. Show me."

"...You're unbelievable. Always have to rub it in when you win."

"And you are still the same idiot I know."

"I've...missed this too."

Khaslana exhaled, his lips hovered in front of Mydeimos. He hesitated, a hand lightly brushing Mydeimos' face.

"You don't have to ask for permission." Mydeimos sighed.

This time, it was the most gentle they had ever been, as if the slightest pressure could break either of them.

"Right. I just don't know how to...after everything. For so long I have longed for your heart—"

Mydeimos laughed.

"You want my heart?"He pointed at Khaslana's chest, "then make yourself one first."

Phainon's eyes snapped open.

It was like waking up from a long, vivid dream. He remembered Mydeimos, and Khaslana. He scanned around, but there's no sign of them.

But then how—

He put a hand over his chest and felt his heartbeat. Strong and steady. There was no scar. No blood. And he felt fine. Better than fine.

And this was when he realized he was also not alone.

"Are you alright?" The voice was somewhat impatient. A tall, blonde man hovered above him. Amber eyes. One side of his hair in braids. In the uniform of a dessert cafe nearby.

His nametag read "Mydei".

"No way." Phainon mumbled.

"I'm leaving." Mydei looked at him like he'd been an idiot. "Clearly there's nothing wrong with you, aside from the sleeping on the ground of a park thing."

"Wait. I'm okay, really. Thank you, Mydei."

"Good," Mydei crossed his arms, "I thought I found a corpse."

"I'm afraid I must disappoint." Phainon smiled, "by the way, this may be a wild guess, but do you like pomegranate juice?"

"How?" Mydei's eyes widened, "how the hell do you know that?"

"Hmm," Phainon grinned, "let's call it fate."

FIN
